subject: computer-science
source_note: Topic structure follows the Eduqas/WJEC GCSE Computer Science specification. Connections, sequence and prerequisites are expert-authored teaching relationships.

units.name: Understanding Computer Science
units.blurb: Theory of hardware, data, networks and society

units.name: Computer Programming
units.blurb: Designing, writing and testing Python programs

topics.name: Hardware
topics.blurb: CPU, Von Neumann architecture, memory and storage

topics.name: Logical Operations
topics.blurb: Logic gates, truth tables and Boolean algebra

topics.name: Data Representation & Storage
topics.blurb: Binary, hex, characters, images, sound and compression

topics.name: Software Development
topics.blurb: IDE tools and the development environment

topics.name: Problem Solving & Design
topics.blurb: Decomposing a problem and designing a solution

topics.name: Data Structures in Code
topics.blurb: Using arrays and records in programs

connections.why: Logic gates are the building blocks of the CPU hardware
The operating system manages the underlying hardware resources
How data is represented in binary underlies how it is organised into structures
Data is encoded into packets and bits for transmission across networks
Boolean logic drives the selection and iteration constructs in algorithms
Algorithms designed in pseudo-code are implemented in Python
Language level determines whether code is compiled or interpreted
Records and arrays studied in theory are used directly when programming
A designed solution is then coded up in Python
Programs are tested and refined after implementation
IDE tools support writing and debugging the program
Sorting and searching algorithms operate on the data structures used
Cybersecurity and data use raise the legal and ethical issues for society
Translators and the OS work together to run a program
Understanding data types underpins how variables are used in code
